sections.title: The dashboard
items: The home page at smcmurry6-source.github.io/study-hubs. Bookmark this, not individual hubs. It was redrawn in November 2026: same address, and your progress, rank, trophies and settings came with you.

Guided tour: A short walk through the dashboard on the real page, ten stops at most. It no longer asks on your first visit. Take the tour in the top bar's menu (the three lines). Each hub has its own tour too.

Your hubs: Every live hub is a tab along the top with its emblem and its exam's countdown, soonest first, the open one in the hub's color. The page opens on the hub whose exam is next, or the one you had open last. The open hub shows its drawn scene across the page, the exam's date, the days left on a tile that flips like a departure board, a bead for each day left (up to two weeks out, ending on the hub's emblem), a ring for your progress in it (questions tried, how many right), and Start studying and Daily drill with today's status. Under it: what the hub covers, its other exams, its "Updated" label and its Timmy Time episode when it has one. A hub archives itself at 10 pm on its last exam day and moves to Past hubs at the bottom for 10 days.
Send luck: The day before an exam and the morning of it (until 2 pm), a row lets you send luck once per exam. It shows how many classmates sent it and the latest names.

You: One card for everything that's yours: the name classmates see, with Pick your name / Change name (everyone starts with a random class name like "Gleaming Molar"); Timmy at his place, in what you put on him; your rank as the card's centerpiece, on dark plum with gold rays turning behind the medallion: its name, your XP counting up, your place in the class, a gold bar to the next level with the next medallion waiting at its end, your mastery medals, and buttons for the Trophy case and The road ahead; your Shiny Gold Crowns with Timmy's Shop; your day streak with the last seven days as dots; and this week's answers with a ring for how many were right. The top bar shows your streak and rank too. The road, under the boards: the three journeys one under the other (Handpiece, ModuPro, Loupes), each opening to its seven ranks on a track that fills in gold as far as you've come, with the XP each rank starts at and its levels I, II and III. Yours is open and marked "You are here"; tap a later journey to see what's waiting.

The class: Studying right now is a drawn classroom: the count on the chalkboard with how many are in each hub, and a Timmy at a desk for everyone who has a hub open, wearing the outfit on at their own Timmy's place (a plain tooth when nothing is on, or with Timmy or the extras off). When someone opens a hub their Timmy hops in through the door and jumps into a desk; when they close it he gets up and leaves. The desk's front is the hub's color, the windows show day or night, rows are added as the room fills, and past a full room a sign by the door says how many are in the hall. No names: nobody can tell which Timmy is anyone else's. Your own Timmy's desk has a "You" plate while you have a hub open in another tab, on your screen only. Reduced motion (or answer animations off) seats them without the walk; Focus mode shows the plain count. The count is in the top bar too. Under it, the leaderboard, one list at a time: Ranks (the top 10, with every rank from Stone to Dark Matter folded under it) or Study streaks, with the top three on a stage: curtains, spotlights, confetti, gold, silver and bronze blocks, a crown for first, and each winner's own Timmy on top in their outfit. Mastery medals show next to every name. Tap anyone to visit their Timmy's place. Today's Golden Probe winner is under the board when there is one. Correct-in-a-row, the arcade high scores (each hub's Arcade keeps its own boards) and the "When people study" chart are no longer on the dashboard.

Idea board: A cork board where every idea is a pinned note: the paper's color and the little picture say what kind it is, the pushpin is in its hub's color (red for all hubs), Sam's answer is stamped on it and the top idea wears a rosette. Post an idea for the hubs and vote on your classmates'. An idea has a title and up to 280 characters, the hub it's for (or all hubs) and what kind it is: a new feature, making something work better, questions and notes, games and fun, look and feel, or something else. It shows to the class right away under your leaderboard name, with its up and down votes. One vote per idea; tap again to take it back. Top, New and Shipped tabs, and filters by hub and by kind. Three ideas a day. Report hides an idea after three reports until Sam looks; you can delete your own, and its votes go with it. Sam marks ideas Under consideration, Planned, Shipped or Not doing with a line on why, and you get that in your Inbox if it's yours or you voted it up. Votes show what the class wants; they don't decide what gets built. No quiz or exam questions or answers, and nothing about a classmate. Its own section on the dashboard; in a hub, under More.

Past hubs: Each finished exam's recap is a drawn card in that hub's color, one exam at a time (chips switch between them): the hours studied together, the classmates as a crowd of teeth, hours per day as a bar graph (the exam day's column with a flag, the most hours labeled, Timmy standing on one), then chips for how many answers were right, the day before the exam, the busiest hour, night owls and regulars, and "the one that got us" when there is one. The numbers count up and the columns grow as you reach it. Save image still gives the shareable picture. Totals only, no names. Above it, Exam check-ins: every check-in still open for a closed hub in one place, each with its exam date and a Check in button, and "Sent" once you've done it.

Exam check-ins: From 8 am on exam day (or once the exam closes, for an exam open all day, like PCD Exam 3 until 8 pm) a "Check in" button appears on the hub card; from 10 pm a pop-up asks once. Special Patient Care has no check-in, because the course doesn't allow discussing its exam with anyone until after November 18. Short questions: how ready you felt, how it went, how the hub compared to the exam, and anything the hub could do better (Occlusion's midterm also asks how helpful the diagrams and the picture Patient Box questions were; PCD Implants also asks whether its new drawn Patient Box cases were better than the Patient Box questions you had before and how helpful its diagrams were, each with an "I didn't use them" button that keeps those who skipped them out of the rating, which of its study tools helped you (tick any), and how it felt that the hub kept changing up to exam day). Please don't write out exam questions or answers, since the honor code keeps exam content private. The answers shape the next hubs. The button is under the open hub from 8 am on exam day, and in the Exam check-ins panel at the top of Past hubs once it archives (every closed hub's open check-in together); the 10 pm pop-up is unchanged, and it waits while a reply to one of your reports is on screen. Under "Anything the hub could do better?" a box, ticked to start, also posts that answer on the idea board under your leaderboard name. You see the post first (its title, text and kind, all yours to change); untick it and the answer goes only to Sam, as before. Your other answers are never posted.
Inbox: Replies to your reports and suggestions (kept 90 days) and notices to the whole class (60 days). The top-bar button shows an unread count; new items pop up once in the bottom right.

Settings and theme: The gear opens Settings: Theme, Text size, Focus mode (the same switch as in a hub: no streak, XP, ranks, boards or Timmy), and the extras (Timmy, hidden secrets, plaque bosses, the Tooth Fairy, the Golden Probe, tactical nukes, rank-up and trophy cards, streak cheers, the streak flame, answer animations). Light or dark is also in the top bar's menu. Font, Background sound and Accent are gone: the redesign has one typeface.

Surveys: At most one short survey (up to 5 questions) is live at a time. It pops up once on the dashboard; tap Later and it waits at the top of your Inbox (on every hub and the dashboard, with a dot on the Inbox button) until you answer it. Where a question offers Other, picking it opens a box to type your own answer.

A top bar that fits your screen: On a narrow phone or at the largest text the dashboard's bar drops, in order, the studying-now count, the words "Study Hubs" and the rank badge. Nothing runs off the screen.
A little something on each hub: Each hub's drawn scene has something to say.

sections.title: In every hub
items: What every hub has, whatever its subject. Most of it is on the hub's bar or under More, where Talk to us holds the Inbox, Suggest, Report, the idea board, the tour, this page and the way back to the dashboard.

Hub tour: Every hub has its own guided tour with a spotlight on the real buttons. No pop-up on arrival any more: a one-line tip shows the first time you open each part of a hub. Take the tour under More (Talk to us).

Search: Searches the full text of the hub (notes paragraphs, review rows, exam hints, cram lines and questions) and jumps to the exact spot. Magic words typed here also work (that's how phones do the easter eggs). The magnifier on the hub's bar.

Daily drill: A set of questions a day per hub, fixed for the day: spaced-review questions that are due, questions you missed last time, then high-yield ones the class finds hard, spread across lectures. Each card says why it was picked. Pick the length before you start: 10, 20 or 30 questions (it remembers your choice). Finish for a results screen (the check draws itself, your score counts up, each question ticks in with a check or an X, and the drill streak rolls up when that set started today's streak), buttons for 10, 20 or 30 more, and a drill streak. Daily drill on a hub's Home, under Questions (the Sets row), the Daily drill button on the dashboard, or …/hubs/<hub>/#questions/drill.

Rewards on every answer: XP counts up on the rank pill in the bar, the goal ring fills, the day-streak flame grows with the streak, and Timmy cheers or flinches. When you leave the questions with 5 or more answered, a session recap card says how it went and offers the misses. It never interrupts practice.

Daily goal: A ring in the bar fills toward your goal: 10 to 50 questions a day (20 to start; change it in Settings). The streak still counts any day you answer a question; missing the goal doesn't break it. On Home, the goal is a ring of 20 teeth that fill in as you answer.

Answer feedback: Answer a question and a wash of green sweeps across the right choice with a soft glow and a check mark that draws itself. A wrong pick shakes and gets an X, then the right answer lights up. Select-all and ordering questions mark each option in turn, matching pairs light up as they lock in, and the explanation slides open. Works wherever you answer questions: the question bank, Weak Spots and the Daily drill.

Streak flame: Get 3 right in a row and a flame appears in the bottom-right corner counting your run, with a ring that fills toward 100 (the tactical nuke). It grows and changes color as you go: orange at 5, red-hot at 10, blue at 25, violet at 50 and gold at 100. Miss one and it fizzles out in a puff of smoke. It counts the run on the page you're on, like the nuke. Off with Settings → Extras → Streak flame, or with Focus mode. (The flame on the hub's bar is a different one: it counts the days in a row you've studied.) It steps aside on the Mock Exam tab.

Smaller touches: Progress bars fill from where they were instead of jumping. Switching modes, tabs and lectures fades the new page in. If your device is set to reduce motion, the hubs keep the check and X marks and the results cards and skip the rest.
Spaced review: Every question you get right comes back after 1, then 2, 4 and 7 days, never later than the day before the exam. Misses come back sooner. It feeds the drill and Weak Spots.
Studying now: The green dot in the bar counts everyone on this hub right now, you included, and Home says it under the countdown. It's a live total: nothing about who.

Focus mode: One switch at the top of Settings turns Timmy and every extra off, for just the notes and the questions. Turning it off brings back what you had, and turning any one extra back on ends it. It uses the extras' own switches, so the dashboard and every hub follow it.

Class accuracy on every question: After you answer, the explanation shows what % of the class got it right. Explanations name the most popular wrong answer when it's a common trap. How the class answered : once you answer a multiple-choice or select-all question, every choice shows the % of the class that picked it, with a light bar behind it, and the most common pick is in bold. A wrong answer with a big share is the trap most people fall for. Your own answer is counted in, and the line under the explanation says how many answers it's based on. In the Question Bank, Weak Spots and the Daily drill in every hub, and on your mock exam's results (never while you're taking it). It shows once at least one other person has answered that question. Every answer counts, so someone who answers a question three times counts three times.

Why each choice: Every multiple-choice and select-all question explains each answer choice, not just the right one. After you answer, tap the folded "Why each choice" bar under the explanation to see why the right answer is right and what is wrong with each of the others, with your pick marked. It starts folded so it doesn't fill the screen. It shows in the Question Bank, the Daily Drill and when you review a mock exam. Every new question gets one too.

Find this in the notes: Miss a question and a Find this in the notes button appears under the explanation. Tap it to read the notes paragraph that matches the question, right there in the card, with its key words marked; Open this in the notes takes you to that spot in the lecture and highlights it. It works in the Question Bank, Weak Spots and the Daily drill (opening the notes closes the drill; it picks up where you left off), not in the mock exam or the arcade. When no paragraph matches well enough, the button doesn't show.

Good question?: Under every explanation, once you answer, a thumbs up or down for the question itself. A thumbs down asks what's wrong with it: the answer looks wrong, the wording is confusing, it isn't in the notes, the explanation didn't help, or it gives the answer away (for anything else, report it opens the Report form). Tap the same thumb again to take your vote back. Together with how the class does on each question (how many get it right the first time, who gets it right after missing it, how long it takes, whether people give up on it or skip the explanation), your votes put questions that may have a problem on a list that gets checked against the notes. Nothing changes a question on its own: a person reads it, and a fix goes out like any other. In the Question Bank, Weak Spots, the Daily drill and your mock exam's results (never while you're taking it), in every hub. One vote per question; it's remembered on this device.
Report an issue: A Report button on every question and under each lecture's notes, plus one under More. When it's fixed you get a reply in your Inbox saying what changed.

Suggest something: Send an idea for the hubs. Replies come back the same way. It's still private, to Sam. Tick Also post this on the idea board to put it on the board too, under your leaderboard name.

Listen: On Lecture Notes: pre-recorded narration of every lecture, at all three reading levels, with seek, ±15 s, speed, resume where you left off, and lock-screen controls. Controls that follow you : scroll away from the Listen button while it's reading and a small player bar stays at the bottom of the screen with play/pause, a progress bar you can drag, the time and a stop button. Tap the lecture's name on it to jump back up. A classmate's idea. Archived hubs : when a hub is archived after its exam, its recorded narration comes off the site (GitHub limits how big the site can be). Listen still works there, in your device's own voice. Follow along : while Listen plays a lecture's narration, the word being read is highlighted in the notes, with its sentence shaded more softly, and the page scrolls to keep it in view. Scroll away and it stops following until you come back (or move the narration: then it jumps there). The Follow along button beside Listen turns it off or back on, on this device. A classmate's idea, from the survey. In a browser too old for it, Listen plays as before, without the highlight.

Highlighter: Select any text in the Lecture Notes and tap Highlight to mark it, or pick a color first: yellow, green, blue, pink or orange . Your last color is remembered, and tapping a highlight lets you change its color. Your highlights stay put when you come back, at that reading level, and Listen still works over them. Tap a highlight to recolor or remove it, or to clear every highlight in those notes. A classmate's idea. Highlights are saved on this device only, so they don't follow you to another phone or laptop. If a lecture's notes get rewritten, its old highlights are cleared rather than landing on the wrong words.

Timmy Time: A podcast episode for the night before the exam, hosted by Timmy Tooth (deep voice, small tooth). He walks through every lecture on the exam in the order the questions are weighted, quotes what the professors said would be tested and what to skip, and finishes with a lightning round where you answer out loud before he does. Music, chapters you can jump between, speeds from 1× to 2×, ±15/30 s, resume where you left off, and lock-screen controls. It keeps playing when you switch tabs or modes, with a small player pinned to the bottom of the screen. Listening counts as study time. Likes and comments : under every episode you can like or dislike it, read what the class thought and add your own comment (it posts under your leaderboard name, up to 280 characters). The thread starts folded to its first comment: tap Show more comments for the rest. Delete your own any time; report anyone else's, and a comment with three reports is hidden until it's checked. A few comments come from Timmy's world (his neighbor number thirty-one, for one): they're the ones with a tag and a dashed border. It's in the quick links on the hub's Home, under More → Timmy Time, and under the hub on the dashboard. Episodes so far: MSK Exam 4 (42 min), the Occlusion midterm (45 min, with Dr. Givan's fence post walked through step by step), Heme & Endo Exam 1 (53 min, all ten lectures gland by gland, with the 10/28 review's answers), PCD Implants Exam 1 (48 min, all nine lectures and every item on the course's hint list) and Heme & Endo Exam 2 (52 min, L11-L16 with the lab patterns the class keeps flipping, the two picture questions, and a quick Exam 1 refresher). The file is big (30 to 40 MB), so it only downloads when you press play. An episode comes off the site with its hub's narration when the hub is archived after the exam.

Moving around the notes: On a laptop the lecture list down the side scrolls on its own, so the last lectures are always one scroll away instead of at the bottom of the notes. At the end of every lecture's notes, Previous and Next take you straight to the lecture before or after it, back at the top. Diagrams you can play with now fit on the screen with their buttons: the drawing stays pinned at the top while its options and explanation scroll up under it, so you can change a setting and watch the drawing at the same time. Report a problem with these notes : a button under each lecture's notes for a typo, a mistake or something confusing in that lecture. It goes to the same place as a question report, and you get a reply in your Inbox when it's fixed. In every hub.

Three ways to read: As taught (the professor's version), Plain English (the same facts in everyday words) and High yield: only what's most likely on the exam. High yield lists each predicted topic (the same list as Exam hints' "Most likely questions"), strongest evidence first, with the part of the notes that teaches it and the professor's own "know this", then what else was flagged in class and what you can skip. Its button at the end opens that lecture's High likelihood questions. Listen reads all three, with Follow along.
Mind maps: "Show mind map" under each lecture draws its outline as a branching tree.

Settings: Focus mode, Theme, Text size (Small to XX-Large), your daily goal, your display name, and the extras, each with its own switch: Timmy Tooth (On / Dashboard only / Off; off, an Ask button takes his place), Hidden secrets (holidays, magic words and the other easter eggs), Plaque bosses, Tooth Fairy, Golden Probe, Tactical nukes (On / Mine only, which hides classmates' strikes / Off), Rank-up and trophy cards, Streak cheers (confetti and a toast every 5 in a row), Streak flame, and Answer animations (off keeps the check and X marks, and stops the pop-ups' and pages' entrances). The same switches in every hub's Settings and the dashboard's. The font choice, background sound and accent metals are gone. The gear on the hub's bar, or More → Settings.
Install as an app: "Add to Home Screen" gives a Gold-handpiece app icon and opens full screen. Pages load from cache when the connection is bad.

What the hubs record: There's no sign-in and no email. Your browser gets a random id, kept on this device, that ties your progress, rank and trophies together (Link my devices joins two browsers). Under that id the hubs save: time in each part of a hub (only while the tab is in view and you've used it in the last 15 minutes), which buttons and tabs you tap, your answers (right or wrong, which choice, whether it was your first try, and how long you spent on the question and on its explanation; a question you read for a few seconds and leave unanswered is noted too), which features you use (Listen, Timmy Time, diagrams, the drill) and which settings you have on, and whatever you send (reports, suggestions, check-ins, surveys, comments, a thumbs up or down on a question). Words typed into Search are saved with no id at all. While you have a hub open, the dashboard's "studying now" count includes you, along with the outfit your Timmy has on, with no name or id; none of that is saved, and it's gone when you close the tab. Nothing else you type is recorded, no IP address, location or device details are saved with your data, and there are no ad or analytics trackers from other companies. It's used to make the hubs better for the whole class: what gets used, which questions trip people up, what to fix before the next exam. Only Sam sees study data per person. Classmates see only what the hubs are built to show: leaderboards, trophies and comments under your leaderboard name (a generated dentistry name unless you pick one), and class-wide numbers such as the share of the class who got a question right. Nothing is used to grade or judge anyone. Clearing this site's data in your browser starts a new id, and your progress on that device goes with it. How long it's kept : time in each part of a hub is saved in 25-second steps for 30 days, then only as hourly totals. Which buttons and tabs you tapped is kept for 90 days, and which features you used for 180 days; after that only class-wide daily totals remain, with no id. A report or suggestion loses your id 120 days after Sam replies (what it said and the reply stay), a survey answer 90 days after the survey closes, and an exam check-in after a year. Your answers, XP, rank and trophies are kept, because your progress is built from them. The cleanup runs by itself once a week. With the redesign: your chats with Ask Timmy are saved, every message with your browser's id, to help improve the hub (Sam reads them on the admin page to fix gaps in the notes and wrong answers). They're answered by Claude, Anthropic's AI: your question, the hub's notes and what's on your screen go to Anthropic's API to write the answer, and nowhere else. Only Sam and your own browser can read your chats; classmates never see them. An idea you post on the idea board shows to the class under your leaderboard name, and so does a check-in's "Anything the hub could do better?" unless you untick the box. Your votes and reports on ideas are kept so each person counts once; nobody else sees who voted or reported. How you rated each flashcard and where you are in Learn are kept, so your schedule and progress follow you to your other devices. What you bought in Timmy's shop and what's out at his place are kept, so they stay yours on every device. Counted, with nothing about who or which: opening Timmy's place and changing something there (which spot, never which piece); opening the shop, a purchase (its kind: an outfit, a snack, a boost, never which piece) and a rare costume turning up; a visit to someone's place (that one happened, never whose); a bowling clip playing (which clip, never who saw it). The clips you've seen and your run of right answers are kept on your device only. The outfit your Timmy has on goes with the studying-now count, with no name or id, and isn't saved.

sections.title: Inside a hub
items: Each hub has four parts on its bar: Home, Notes, Questions and More. On a laptop the bar is at the top; on a phone it's at the bottom, with a Settings button beside the four. Your answers, pins, highlights and progress in each hub carried over from the old pages.
Back to the dashboard: Always on the screen in a hub: All hubs at the start of the bar on a laptop, Hubs at the start of the top strip on a phone. (More → All hubs is still there.)

Pages and pop-ups move: A hub's pages slide in from the side their tab is on, the tab you tapped pops, a hub's panel on the dashboard slides in the same way, and every pop-up window (the shop, Timmy's place, the trophy case, the Inbox, a check-in, a survey) rises into place. Off with your device's reduced-motion setting or Settings → Answer animations.

Home: Every hub opens on its own Home: the hub's masthead, the exam card (a live countdown and the announced facts), quick links on the first phone screen (practice questions, Daily drill, the notes you were on, the mock, and Timmy Time when the hub has an episode), Where to next (at most three: yesterday's misses in exam week, your weakest lecture, a lecture not started), Today (the goal as a ring of 20 teeth, your streak, XP today, right today, Timmy's HP), progress by lecture with Notes and Questions buttons, and the course timeline. Under the countdown: how many are studying this hub right now.

Notes: The lecture list (lectures on the exam first, the others for review, each with a progress bar and how many questions you've tried), three reading levels (As taught, Plain English, High yield), Listen with Follow along, the drawn diagrams beside their paragraph, each lecture's charts under its notes, and Check yourself: three questions at the end of each lecture's notes. At the end, Previous lecture / Next lecture, and Report a mistake in these notes (also in the notes toolbar), which opens the report form with the lecture attached.

Questions: The Question Bank, its filter panel (with the High likelihood toggle) and four sets: Daily drill, Yesterday's misses, Weak spots and Mock exam. Answer choices are plain rows with a check or a cross after you answer; Pin and Report are on every card. After an answer, one row: Try it again, Find this in the notes (on a miss), Ask Timmy and Good question?.

Study as: Questions, Learn or Flashcards: At the top of Questions. The panel picks which questions; this picks how. Learn and Flashcards show a card with how far along you are and a Start button, then take the whole screen, one card at a time, like Quizlet: a Close button (or Escape) puts you back in the bank, and your progress is kept. Learn asks the questions you picked in rounds of 7 until you've got each right twice (the second time, when the question allows it, you think of the answer before the choices show; a miss comes back at the end of the round). The choices are big tiles (keys 1 to 6 pick one on a laptop), Don't know? shows the answer without a guess, and after a right answer it moves on by itself unless you touch the card to read why (the Auto-next switch turns that off). A bar along the top shows how far along you are, and each round ends with what you got. Flashcards show the question on a card; you flip it (Flip the card, a tap on the card or the space bar) and say how well you knew it: Again, Hard, Good or Easy, keys 1 to 4, the left and right arrows for Again and Good, or on a phone a swipe left for Again and right for Good. It comes back when you're about to forget it, never later than the day before the exam. When you're caught up you see how the session went, rating by rating. Home tells you when cards are due. Learn's answers count like any answer. A flashcard counts toward your daily goal and streak (not as an answer: no class stats, no "Last time") and earns 2 XP when it's due or new, for its first three ratings a day; Study ahead earns none. Drill, Yesterday's misses and Weak spots work in all three; the mock exam is always questions.

Question types: Multiple choice, select-all with partial credit, matching, ordering, two-statement, EXCEPT / NOT, Patient Box cases and picture questions, each in the exam's own format. Which statement is true, or false? : four full statements, and you pick the one true statement (or, in the inverse, the one false statement among three true ones). Each false statement changes one detail you were taught, never a trick of wording, and every choice explains itself once you answer. Find them under the Question Bank's More filters → question type (Heme & Endo Exam 2 and Occlusion's final lectures for now; every new lecture gets them). Patient pictures : some Patient Box cases in Heme & Endo now show an illustration of the findings the box lists (the gums in Addison's disease, the face and hands in acromegaly, a patient on long-term prednisone). They're painted for the hub, not photos of real patients, and they only show what the box already says, so they never give the answer away. Patient cases drawn from their numbers : in the Perio and PCD Implants hubs, Patient Box cases now come with a periodontal chart, a periapical radiograph and a drawn view of the gums, all produced from the same case numbers (probing depths, recession, bleeding, mobility, furcations, bone levels, restorations, implants), the way the Perio midterm check-ins asked. Every tooth is drawn from its real anatomy (the sizes and shapes in Wheeler's Dental Anatomy: the right cusps, the right number of roots, the long canine root, the root trunk above a molar's furcation), and every number in a case is checked to be realistic and to agree with the others before it ships. The chart is drawn like a probing chart (blue line for the gingival margin, red line for the pocket base, red dots for bleeding, furcation triangles), with the numbers in a table under it. Everything you need to answer is in the box before you answer, and a picture never shows the answer: a question that asks you to work out the attachment level hides the CAL row, one that asks the furcation class hides the furcation row. After you answer, "Why each choice" explains every option and In the notes buttons jump to the notes paragraph and Review table the case comes from. The drawings are illustrations made from the numbers, never patient photos or real radiographs. The first six cases cover staging and grading, gingivitis versus periodontitis, recession types, a furcation, a regeneration candidate and an implant; more are coming. Numbered statements : in the Heme & Endo and Occlusion hubs (and Perio from Session 7 on , and every hub from now on, at least two per lecture), "Which statements are true? 1... 2... 3... 4..." questions answered with a combination ("1, 2 and 4", "2 and 3 only"), the way Dr. Givan's midterm asked them. The combinations always come in the same order, the Question Bank's format filter has them too, and after you answer, "Why each choice" says which statement each wrong combination got wrong. Heme & Endo also has two-statement and true-or-false questions for every lecture, and Perio now has true-or-false questions too (Sessions 7 and 8; the Question Bank's type filter has "True or false" and "Numbered statements"). High Likelihood Exam Questions : in the Heme & Endo Exam 1 hub, questions on the topics most likely to be on the exam carry a "High Likelihood Exam Question" tag. The predictions combine how many exam questions each lecture gets with what the professors flagged in the recordings and asked at the in-class review. The Question Bank's new sort menu can put them first (High likelihood first) or show only them, and Exam Hints opens with a folded Most likely questions list: each lecture's count on the exam and its predicted topics, with a button to practice them. It's an educated guess, not a leak: nobody has seen the exam. Its mock exam now uses the exam's real count per lecture and, like the exam, puts all four Patient Box questions on L4. Two-statement and true or false in Occlusion : the Occlusion hub now has two-statement questions (decide whether each of two statements is true) and true-or-false questions, one set per lecture. Their choices always stay in the same order. The Question Bank's new format filter shows just one kind at a time: two statements, true or false, EXCEPT / NOT, Patient Box or select all. Patient cases with findings : in the Occlusion hub, "a patient comes in with this... what do you do?" cases show their findings as images: periodontal charts, periapical, bitewing and TMJ radiographs, intraoral photos, articulating-paper marks, shimstock tests, mounted casts and a bite record. They are drawings made for the hub, not real patient images. When one patient has several things worth testing, two to four questions share the same box and findings : the box says "Same patient · 2 of 3", and the Question Bank keeps that patient's questions together, even when you shuffle.

What cusp hits where?: A quick game at the top of the Occlusion Question Bank, built on Dr. Givan's help sheet. Contacts: a cusp is lit on one arch; tap the fossa it lands in on the other (Class I, II and III, right and left sides). Then the lower teeth slide into their class position, every contact line appears and the fence post shows why. Movements: "What is the cusp and motion in this picture?" Name the movement an arrow shows, then the cusp that made it. 10 rounds; your best score is kept on this device. Rounds don't count toward class stats. Stuck? "Show the fence post" draws the one for that class before you answer.

Question Bank filters: The Question Bank's filters sit in one labeled panel above the questions. Lectures (Perio: Sessions) opens a list with a tick box per lecture, so you can practice any mix; tap Only on a row for just that one (Occlusion adds For the final and Midterm lectures). Show picks All, Not answered yet, Missed last time or Pinned, and each chip says how many questions you'd get. Only, under it, is the High likelihood tick box, which works on top of whichever Show chip you picked: tick it with Missed last time for the likely-exam questions you got wrong, with Not answered yet for the ones you haven't tried, with Pinned for the ones you saved, or with All for every one of them. Tap it again to turn it off. Order is In order (lecture by lecture) or Random (tap it again to reshuffle). More filters adds the question type (true or false, two statements, Patient Box, matching and the rest) and where a question comes from. Under the panel, a line says how many questions are showing and lists every filter that's on: tap one to take it off, or Clear all. If nothing matches, it says which filter is in the way and gives you a button back to the whole bank. In the Occlusion, Perio, Special Patient Care and PCD Implants hubs, and every hub built from now on. The bank opens with the lectures, filters and order you used last time (the search box starts empty), and the line under the panel shows them, so you always know what's hidden. A Sets row under Show: Daily drill, Yesterday's misses, Weak spots and Mock exam. A set replaces the list until you close it; your filters stay as they were. On a laptop a Today column (the goal ring, streak, XP, this session) sits beside the questions.

High Likelihood Exam Questions: Each hub predicts the topics most likely to be on its exam, lecture by lecture, from what the professors flagged in the recordings, in-class reviews and focus lists, the class exam-review guide and what earlier check-ins said the exam asked. The questions on those topics carry a High Likelihood Exam Question tag in the Question Bank and the Daily drill (never in the mock exam, which stays exam-like). Each topic shows where it came from. In Heme & Endo Exam 2, the exam's five Exam 1 questions come from Exam 1's L2, L3, L6 and L10, so the Exam 1 Refresher tags those four lectures' High Likelihood questions (and holds only those four lectures' questions), the mock's five Exam 1 questions follow the split the class was given (two from L2, one on which hormones work synergistically, one on how PTH maintains blood calcium, one more), each drawn at random from them, and the Question Bank has an Exam 1 High likelihood tick box beside High likelihood for practicing just those. They're there for review, so they don't count in that hub's totals or its mastery medal. Open Exam Hints → Most likely questions for the list, with a Practice these button per lecture. In the Question Bank, tick High likelihood (the Only line, under Show) to practice only those questions , together with Not answered yet, Missed last time or Pinned if you like; untick it for the whole bank. In every live hub and every hub built from now on.

Pinned questions: Every question card has a Pin button next to Report. Pin the ones you want to come back to, and the Question Bank's Pinned chip (under Show) shows only those, still with your lecture picks and order. Tap Pinned again on a card to unpin it. In the Occlusion, Perio, Special Patient Care and PCD Implants hubs, and every hub built from now on. Pins follow you to your other devices once they're linked (Stats → Link my devices); an unpin on one device unpins it everywhere.

Missed it? Try it again: In every hub's Question Bank, a question you miss comes back as a fresh card five questions further down the list, marked Try it again, so you get a second rep while it is still fresh instead of only at the end (or through the "Missed last time" filter). Miss it again and it comes back again. A patient's questions stay together, so it never lands in the middle of a case. A classmate's idea.

Undo on ordering questions: Tapped a step by mistake? Undo last step takes back your latest tap and Start over clears them all. Both show up once you've tapped a step and go away when the question is graded.

Diagrams: In the Occlusion hub, drawn diagrams sit right inside the Lecture Notes, next to the paragraph they explain (and in Review; every one, and every Patient Box picture, checked against the notes and redrawn where it was off, with the side views on a whole skull and labels in the lecture's own words):the envelope of motion in three planes, cusp pathways on #3 and #30, which cusp inclines collide, and a fence post and contact map with Class I, II and III tabs that shows where every cusp lands, the way the "What cusp hits where?" help sheet draws it. Each one has a folded Show the key under it (what arrow A, B, C and D are, what each border, point or incline is), so you can test yourself first. About 20 questions ask you to read one, the way the exam does ("the MIP contact is at the base of the arrow"): the key stays hidden until you answer, then the explanation shows the diagram with its key open . The PCD Fixed Pros Exam 3 hub has them too: the Munsell color solid, additive vs subtractive color, specular vs diffuse reflection, veneer prep designs and the dog leg, the papilla rule, crown-sectioning cut paths and the bonding "Lego" chain. Heme & Endo Exam 2 has numbered drawings of its exam's two picture questions: the Sertoli cell (L13) and the five follicle stages (L14), each laid out like the professor's picture, with a key to test yourself and picture questions in the Question Bank. Interactive diagrams : in the Occlusion hub, TMJ opening (L2 notes and Review) lets you open the mouth from 0 to 50 mm with a slider or Play: the condyle first only rotates inside the disc (lower joint space) up to about 20-25 mm, when the outer TM ligament goes taut; then the condyle and disc slide down the eminence (upper joint space) while the disc turns back on the condyle and the retrodiscal tissue fills in behind. The inferior head of the lateral pterygoid lights up as you open, the superior head as you close, and every part explains itself when tapped. Cusp pathways in motion (L1 notes next to the cusp pathways, and Review → Review of Basic Occlusion, under What cusp hits where): pick protrusive, working, non-working or retrusive and watch the opposing cusp leave its MIP contact on #3 and on #30 at the same time, so you can see every path reverse on the lower tooth (A-D match the key). Below it, the jaw seen from above swings around the working condyle; sliders move the cusp farther from the condyle or the midline, widen the intercondylar distance or add a side shift, and the angle between the working and non-working paths opens or closes the way the notes say. Working and non-working interferences (L1 notes next to the help sheet method, and Review under What cusp hits where): slide the lower right molar toward the cheek (a right move) or the tongue (a left move) in the front-view section, and the inclines that can collide light up by number (2 with 6 and 4 with 5 working, 1 with 3 non-working) with a spark where they touch; a side-view tab does protrusion (mandibular mesial inclines on maxillary distal inclines), and "Let the guidance lift the teeth apart" shows why there's no interference when the canines or incisors do their job. Muscles by movement (L2 notes after the exam slide table, and Review → Functional TMJ Anatomy): pick elevation, depression, protrusion, retrusion or a move to the right or left, and the muscles on Dr. Givan's exam slide light up on a side view of the skull, each with an arrow along its line of pull (the superficial layer, then a deep view with the zygomatic arch taken off for the two heads of the lateral pterygoid and the medial pterygoid). For a move to one side, flip to the patient's other side to see the other half of the slide. Tap any muscle for where it attaches and what it does. What sets posterior cusp height (L1 notes after the determinants table, and Review → Guidance and determinants): sliders for condylar guidance, vertical and horizontal overlap, the plane of occlusion and the curve of Spee. A dashed outline shows the tallest cusp that would still clear, and cusps taller than that turn red. Then protrude the jaw (or press Protrude): the condyle comes down the eminence, the lower incisor comes down the upper one, and the gap that opens between the back teeth is Christensen's phenomenon. Envelope of motion, traced (L1 notes after the envelope figures, and Review under Envelope of motion): press Next step or Play all and a pen on the lower incisor draws the envelope border by border, in the order the notes give it, with each step explained. On the sagittal view a small joint shows the condyle seated, rotating, then sliding down the eminence; tabs switch to the horizontal and frontal views. From CR to the CO contact, then the slide into MIP (L1 notes at MIP, centric occlusion and centric relation, and Review under Positions and terms): press Close and the jaw hinges shut with the condyles seated until the second molars touch (CO), then slides up and forward into MIP while the condyle comes off its seat, with ×4 close-ups of the molars and the joint. "CO = MIP" shows the 10% with no slide. Canine guidance or group function (L1 notes at Guidance and the goals of ideal occlusion, L5 notes at Schemes and guidance, and Review in both lectures): move the jaw to the right, seen from the cheek with a small front view of the canines. With canine guidance only #6 and #27 touch and every back tooth lifts apart; with group function #7, #6 and #5 share the contact and the back teeth only just separate. The text says when each is chosen. Swallowing, stage by stage (L3 notes after Part 2: swallowing, and Review): step a bolus through the three stages in a midline view of the mouth and throat. The tongue presses it back; the soft palate seals the nose, the hyoid rises, the epiglottis covers the trachea and the Eustachian tubes open; then it travels down the esophagus. A toggle compares the adult somatic swallow (teeth in MIP) with the visceral (infantile) swallow, tongue forward between the teeth. A tooth and an implant under load (L5 notes at Implants, and Review): push a natural tooth and an implant with the same force, down or sideways. The tooth sinks about 28 µm on its ligament, which feels it; the implant moves about 2-3 µm. Then run the shimstock check on a light closure and a clench to see why implant crowns are built light. For the final, Occlusion's L6 adds four , in the notes and in Review: where a mounting error shows ( redrawn: a semi-adjustable arcon articulator to scale with both casts in Class I occlusion; mount them too far back, too high, too far forward or too low, protrude, and see tooth by tooth how many microns more or less the back teeth separate on the articulator than in the mouth, set the size of the error, and which teeth then meet early), record thickness and the hinge axis (thicken a CR record and watch the articulator's arc of closure drift from the patient's, then take it at the treatment vertical or use a kinematic facebow), why protrusive records are preferred (set the articulator from a protrusive or a lateral record, or 30° or 20°, and protrude: the crown discludes or hits) and where to take a lateral record (the Bennett angle read at 3-5 mm versus 7-10 mm, and the fossa a crown gets from each). Occlusion's L7 adds five , in the notes and in Review: the tolerance model (stack a high crown, a burned palate, bruxism, deep pain, stress or the flu on normal function and move the tolerance line: below it the patient adapts; above it the signs light up where they show, from pulpitis to headache; "Monday, then Tuesday" replays the same events against a tolerance that dropped), orthopedic vs occlusal stability (seat the joints and close until one tooth touches first, then bite into MIP and watch a condyle come off its seat; change how far MIP is from CR, add a bruxer's loading, or add a flat plane splint that gives both), splint designs (maxillary or mandibular, full or partial, stabilizing or repositioning; protrude on the ramp, or wear a partial splint for months and watch the covered teeth go in and the others come out), the rule of thirds (slide the lower molar off its ideal and see where the upper palatal cusp lands: the first third means selective grinding, the middle third minor orthodontics and fixed prosthetics, beyond that major orthodontics, surgery and prosthetics) and erosion patterns (pick GERD and the side slept on, bulimia, soda swished or pooled, citrus sucked or chewed, or cervical notches, and see which surfaces of which teeth wear, beside a worn molar that compares attrition with erosion). Occlusion's L8 adds four , in the notes and in Review: how the ridges resorb (take the teeth out and run the years forward, in a side view of the front of the mouth and a section through the first molars: the maxilla goes up and in, the mandible down and out; then set denture teeth near the ridges and the back teeth end up in crossbite and the front reads pseudo-Class III), support, stability and retention (pick one to see the force it resists on a pair of complete dentures and what resists it: the palate and buccal shelf, a good fit with a border seal and saliva, the ridge walls and the palatal vault), balanced, non-balanced and lingualized (close, slide into a right working movement or protrude, and watch which sides touch; then try contact on one side only and watch the lower denture tip off its ridge) and posterior tooth forms (anatomic, semi-anatomic, flat and lingualized molars side by side: slide them sideways and see which ones push the denture sideways). Occlusion's L9 adds four , in the notes and in Review: abfraction (move the load from the long axis onto an inclined plane and the tooth bends about the bone like a pushed stop sign, squeezed on one side and stretched on the other; load it again and again and a notch grows on the stretched side, just above the bone), cupped-out cusp tips (wear a molar's cusps down until a pinpoint of dentin shows, then compare wear alone, a flat facet, with wear plus acid, where the exposed dentin dissolves into a cup; a pH scale beside it shows why: dentin starts to dissolve at a higher pH than enamel), pH vs buffering capacity (two drinks, both at pH 4: add bicarbonate a drop at a time and count how much each takes to reach neutral, or add water and watch the pH barely move) and L7's erosion map again, opened on vomiting (the lingual of the upper teeth: the lip guards the facial surfaces and the tongue the lower teeth), with the NCCL view one tap away. Occlusion's L10 adds five , in the notes and in Review: primary vs secondary occlusal trauma (a premolar with normal or reduced support under a normal or traumatic force: with bone lost, the center of rotation drops toward the apex and the same push tips it, like his fence post with only a third in the ground), unilateral vs jiggling force (push one way to tip or move the tooth, or jiggle it back and forth and watch the ligament widen on both sides into an hourglass), the radiographic signs (a film of #28-#30: turn on a widened PDL space, a thickened or broken lamina dura, vertical, furcation or circumferential bone loss and root resorption, each with his warning that none of them proves occlusal trauma), measuring mobility (the tooth between two instrument handles, drawn to scale with a millimeter ruler: degrees 0 to 3 on his scale, pressing for vertical movement, and fremitus) and the animal experiments (add jiggling trauma, gingivitis or periodontitis, or stop the trauma, and see what happened to the attachment, the bone's height and density, the ligament and mobility, with the dogs and the monkeys side by side where they disagreed). The Heme & Endo Exam 1 hub has six , each in the notes next to the section it explains and in that lecture's Review tab: how a beta cell releases insulin (L5: step from glucose through GLUT2 to ATP, the K-ATP channel closing, depolarization, calcium and insulin release; low glucose and a sulfonylurea toggle), making thyroid hormone (L4: the seven steps in a follicular cell, from NIS to secretion, with where methimazole or PTU and an iodide load block it, and what low iodide does; the TSH receptor and the deiodinases are in it now too), the HPA axis and its labs (L2, L6 and L7: normal, Addison's, Cushing's disease, an adrenal tumor and prednisone taken, stopped suddenly or tapered, with the feedback loops, the skin darkening with α-MSH and a lab panel that reads primary or secondary), who moves blood calcium (L10: calcium falling or rising, primary hyperparathyroidism, and a soda habit (high phosphate) and menopause, with PTH, calcitriol and calcitonin acting on kidney, gut and bone), two lobes, two routes (L1 and L2: a releasing hormone through the portal veins to its target cell, or ADH and oxytocin down the long axons, with Herring bodies and pituicytes) and the adrenal from capsule to medulla (L6 and L9: the zones with their shares and products, blood running from cortex to medulla, a view that lights up the medulla's dual blood supply, and a stress response turning on PNMT). Tap any part for what it is. The MSK Exam 4 hub has two you can play with, under the notes and in Review (the junction under Drugs, the sarcomere under Muscle). The neuromuscular junction (L32): pick no drug, succinylcholine, rocuronium, rocuronium reversed by neostigmine or by sugammadex, or botulinum toxin, and watch where it acts, what happens to the end plate, the Na+ channels and the muscle, and how the train of four looks. The sliding sarcomere (L31): drag the slider (or press Play) and the thin filaments slide toward the M line while the I and H bands shrink and the A band stays put. Tap any part for what it is. Seven picture questions in that hub show one of them with a part highlighted, and an in-class review question uses a drawn block of skin (epidermis, dermis, hypodermis, a hair follicle with its sebaceous gland and arrector pili, a sweat gland and the blood vessels) with one structure labeled . PCD Implants Exam 1 : eleven interactive diagrams in the Lecture Notes and Review ( all eleven checked against the notes and redrawn where they were off). Tooth vs implant (fibers, epithelium and bone, each layer to scale, with the 2.04 vs 3.08 mm biologic width), one-stage vs two-stage surgery step by step, Misch's D1-D4 bone and where it is, a cantilever you can slide out to watch a 25 lb bite grow to 75 lb on the implant (and fix with another implant), the ideal implant position (push two implants closer than 3 mm and the papilla drops into a black triangle), connections and platform switching (where the microgap sits), the stability dip week by week, the emergence profile's E, B and C zones (an upper incisor, so coronal is down as in the notes: make the E zone concave or convex and watch the margin move), screw or cement? (a molar crown in section: drag the clearance past 5 mm, tilt the implant facially and see where the screw hole would come out), how a cone beam CT works (the rotating gantry vs a medical CT's fan beam, and the detector layer by layer) and freehand vs pilot-guided vs fully guided vs dynamic. The L1 notes also draw the seven old implant types : all seven now, the intramucosal insert included, each the way it turns up (a panoramic or periapical radiograph, or the tissue side of the denture) with numbered parts in a folded key and, beside it, a section through the jaw showing where it sits: on the bone, through it, in a slot, in the mucosa or in the bone. Seven questions ask you to name one from its drawing; the section and the key stay hidden until you answer. Perio has twelve , under the Session 7, 8 and 9 notes and in Review: peri-implant health, mucositis and peri-implantitis (one implant drawn to scale in a section through the ridge, in its three 2017 states: the mucosa, the bleeding and pus, the probe depth against its baseline, and the bone against the line of initial remodeling), ailing, failing, failed (Meffert's classes on drawn radiographs, each read against the bone on the previous film, with what you do for each), bleeding on probing over four visits (30% down to 1.5%, from Lang 1986), when to take implant radiographs (a timeline from placement to yearly, with the baseline marked and the extra film you take only when the signs change), why a biofilm beats antibiotics (step through the barrier, β-lactamase and slowed growth, then see what scaling and root planing changes) where each antibiotic acts (pick a drug to light its target on the bacterium, and see whether it kills or only stops growth) and the host response, and host modulation (Dr. Litz's flowchart as a cycle that feeds itself, from the bacteria to the host response, cytokines and prostaglandins, tissue and bone breakdown and deeper pockets; take the bacteria away, or pick scaling and root planing, NSAIDs, bisphosphonates or Periostat to see where each breaks the cycle and why only one is approved). From Session 9: the Cairo recession types (one canine with the same recession as RT1, RT2 and RT3, and how much root a graft can cover in each), the palate as a donor site (its layers, and how close the greater palatine artery and nerve run in a shallow, average or high palate), covered or exposed: which graft (step through a connective tissue graft under a coronally advanced flap and a free gingival graft left exposed), altered passive eruption (pick Type 1 or 2 and A or B, then see the crown lengthening each gets) and a gummy smile: find the cause (move the lip length and mobility sliders or lengthen the lower face and see which cause it points to and how it is treated). Tap any part for what it is. On a phone, the radiograph timeline turns into a list and the Meffert films show one at a time. Heme & Endo Exam 2 : nine you can play with, in the Lecture Notes next to the section they explain and in each lecture's Review. Where each diabetes drug acts (L11: pick a drug class and the organs it works on light up, with its mechanism, route, hypoglycemia risk and weight effect), the insulins (L11: rapid, short, intermediate, long and ultra-long-acting curves on one clock, and a basal-bolus day with a "Skip lunch" switch), primary or secondary? Read the labs (L12a and L12b: one feedback loop for the thyroid, cortisol, aldosterone and the parathyroid; pick a disease and a lab slip fills in, or try a mystery case and make the call yourself), congenital adrenal hyperplasia (L12b: block 21- or 17-hydroxylase on the steroid pathway and step through what piles up, why ACTH rises and how glucocorticoids fix it), the seminiferous tubule (L13: follow one spermatogonium to a sperm, with LH, FSH and feedback views), the duct system (L13: move a sperm from the tubule to the urethra, each segment with its lining and job, and a vasectomy switch), follicle stages (L14: primordial to corpus albicans in section, with the oocyte's meiotic arrest at each step and a fertilization switch), the 28-day cycle (L14 and L16: drag the day and watch FSH and LH, the feedback, the ovary, estradiol and progesterone and the endometrium move together; a Pregnancy switch keeps the corpus luteum) and the male HPG axis (L15: GnRH pulses, testosterone's and inhibin's brakes, and eight cases from continuous GnRH to androgen insensitivity). Tap any part for what it is.
Submit at the bottom: Mock exams now have a second Submit exam button (with the answered count) after the last question, so you don't have to scroll back to the top to hand it in.

Mock exam results: Submit a mock exam and a results card opens: your score counts up while a ring fills (gold at 90%+, green at 75%+), a one-line verdict, your best mock in that hub on this device ("New personal best, up from 72%"), and a bar per lecture so you can see where the misses were. 90% or better gets a celebration. "See what I missed" jumps straight to the questions you got wrong; "Review answers" shows them all.

More: A tile per part, each on its own color with a line of what's in it: Timmy Time (the big one, Timmy in headphones), Exam hints, Cram sheet, Side by side (the charts that compare across lectures; it was Review), Arcade, Timmy's place, Timmy's shop, Stats and trophies and Settings. Then Talk to us: Inbox, Suggest something, Report a problem, the Idea board, Take the tour, About and All hubs.

Perio: Review is gone as a tab: each session's tables sit under its notes ("Charts for this lecture") and the search finds their rows. The mock exam follows the final's format from Dr. Abou-Arraj's midterm emails: 46 questions in 80 minutes, 5 Patient Box cases, 5 multiple-answer questions scored with partial credit and 1 ordering question, from all 9 sessions; the results give points per session. Recall cards (Perio's short-answer questions) are in the bank: think of the answer, reveal it, then say whether you got it; that counts as right or missed. Your saved progress, Perio's trophies and its six arcade games carried over as they were.

Arcade: Under More. The lobby shows every game, each on its own color with its own drawing, the hub's pick first (Occlusion: Cusp Sort; Perio: Pocket Showdown). Six games per hub (next part), with the option to play only the questions you missed. Games built on the question bank count toward your stats, XP and Timmy's health.

Older hubs: Hubs that were archived before the redesign (and Heme & Endo Exam 2, whose exam was the day it shipped) keep their old pages: four modes in the top bar (Home, Compendium, Review, Arcade) and the study tools in the launcher at the bottom right. Everything in Part 2 that isn't marked new works there the same way.

sections.title: Arcade games
items: Every game has a class-wide high-score board. In Occlusion and Perio the arcade is under More, and its lobby shows every game on its own color with its own drawing. The Occlusion and Perio arcades now have six games each instead of nine. They share the same rules but each hub has its own look: the Occlusion games are drawn in articulating paper and set in an occlusion lab, the Perio games on a perio chart and in a perio clinic. The Heme & Endo Exam 1 hub's Feedback Loop Arcade has the same six kinds of game, stained like a histology slide and set in an endocrine lab. The Special Patient Care hub's Sparks Arcade has the same six, set in the Sparks Clinic after hours. The PCD Implants hub's Osseo Arcade has them too, in titanium blue, set in the implant lab at night. The Heme & Endo Exam 2 hub's Cycle Arcade has the same six in aubergine and gold, set in the endocrine pathology lab after hours. The action games almost nobody played (snake, flappy, whack-a-mole and the rest) are gone, and three new quiz games came out of your survey answers. In every game built on the question bank, Questions from picks a lecture or Questions I missed, which replays only the ones you got wrong last time.

Occlusion: Freeway Space Arcade · Perio: Pocket Arcade · Heme & Endo: Feedback Loop Arcade · Special Patient Care: Sparks Arcade · PCD Implants: Osseo Arcade · Heme & Endo 2: Cycle Arcade · What it is

Freeway Showdown · Pocket Showdown · Axis Showdown · Chart Showdown · Platform Showdown · Surge Showdown · A Jeopardy-style board: one column per lecture, $100 (the question the class gets right most) to $500 (the toughest). Right adds the value, wrong takes it away. Two tiles hide a wager round, and a final question lets you bet it all. In Occlusion the tiles are articulating-paper strips (Centric Double, Final Contact); in Perio they are teeth on a perio chart that bleed when you miss (Deep Pocket, Final Probe); in Heme & Endo they are glass slides that stain purple or pink (Hormone Surge, Final Feedback); in Special Patient Care they are patient charts (Count to Ten, Final Consent); in PCD Implants they are healing abutments (Torque Check, Final Torque); in Heme & Endo Exam 2 they are capped sample tubes in a rack (LH Surge, Final Surge).

Lab Escape · Perio Clinic Escape · Endo Lab Escape · Sparks After Hours · Implant Lab Escape · Path Lab Escape · A point-and-click escape room. The door locked behind you; tap things in the room and answer the questions that lock them to find the four digits of the door code. Six minutes, and every wrong answer costs 20 seconds.

Mind the Gap · Mind the Pocket · Fill the Receptor · Say It Once · Mind the Microgap · Blank Rx · Fill in the blank, Anki cloze style: a sentence straight from the lecture notes with a key term taken out. Type it before the clock runs down (a typo of a letter or two still counts). Three lives. In Perio the clock is a probe running out of millimeters.

Million-Dollar Smile · Million-Dollar Smile · The Golden Gland · Sparks Superstar · The Golden Fixture · The Yellow Body · Quiz show: 12 rungs to $125,000, three lifelines (50:50, Ask the class, Swap). In The Golden Gland a thyroid turns gold from rung 6; in The Golden Fixture an implant anodizes gold; in The Yellow Body a follicle ripens into a golden corpus luteum.
Cross-Section · Cross-Section · Cross-Stain · Cross-Check · Cross-Slice · Crossing Over · A fresh mini crossword every game, from the course terms.

Cusp Sort · Calculus Crusher · Feedback Sort · Chairside Sort · Osseo Sort · Lab Sort · Cusp Sort, Feedback Sort, Chairside Sort, Osseo Sort and Lab Sort: fling falling cards into the right bin (working or non-working side? hyper- or hypothyroid? active or passive stabilization? screw- or cement-retained? Sertoli or Leydig?). Calculus Crusher: Breakout, hit the brick with the right answer.

The archived MSK Exam 3 and 4 and PCD Exam 3 hubs keep their original nine games (sort, snake, stack, memory match, hangman, true-or-swapped rush, blaster, word search and whack-a-mole, each reskinned for that exam) for as long as their pages stay up.

sections.title: Ranks, mastery and recognition
items: XP: 10 XP the first time you get a question right, 2 for any other right answer, 1 for a miss, and a flat 2 for a card you grade yourself, plus 20 for every day you study. There is no daily cap any more. A question pays for its first three right and its first three wrong answers each day, and answers less than 2 seconds apart (or more than 30 in a minute) still count but earn nothing. Counted across every hub.

More ways to earn XP: +30 at your 20th answer of the day; +5 the first time you get right a question you missed on an earlier day; +50 for a mock exam with 10 or more answers (once a hub a day); +50 for finishing an arcade game (each game once a day, after 20 seconds of play); 10 for each minute of a Timmy Time episode you hear for the first time (most of the minute, up to twice as fast) and +100 for finishing it; +100 when a report or suggestion you sent is fixed; and +100, +200, +300 and +500 for a hub's Bronze, Silver, Gold and Crown medals.

Double XP: Every new mastery medal starts 24 hours of double XP on answers, the day's bonuses, mocks and games (never more than 2x; a new medal starts the 24 hours again). A gold "2x" chip on your rank shows the time left, and the XP that flies up from an answer says "2x". Timmy's shop sells one-hour and three-hour boosts too.

Three journeys: The handpiece ladder is the first of three. Handpiece: Stone (start), Antique (300 XP), Bronze (1,500), Silver (5,000), Gold (12,000), Diamond (25,000), Dark Matter (50,000). At 125,000 XP the ModuPro begins (the sim-lab typodont), and at 250,000 the Loupes, each with the same seven ranks, evenly spaced, each rank with levels I, II and III. Nothing is lost on the way: your XP, trophies and Timmy's place come with you. From the ModuPro on your rank reads "ModuPro Gold II". The road on the dashboard lays all three out, rank by rank, and More → Stats and trophies shows the road ahead too.

Rank-up celebrations: A new rank plays a full-screen cutscene (your old medallion charges up, a flash, the new one), and a new level flips in like a coin, each with the journey's own object. Two more full-screen scenes: reaching Dark Matter opens a starfield inside the medallion (once per journey, ever, on whichever device gets there first; each journey has its own sky), and finishing a journey hands you the next object: "The ModuPro is yours." All of them can be skipped, wait until a mock exam is over, are one still card with reduced motion, and are off with Settings → Extras → Rank-up and trophy cards.
Hub mastery: The share of a hub's question bank you got right on your latest try: Bronze 50%, Silver 75%, Gold 90%, Crown 100%.

Mastery medals: Each hub you master earns a medal of its own: the metal is the tier (Bronze, Silver, Gold, or Gold with a crown on top for Crown), and the emblem and ribbons belong to the hub (a probe for Perio, meeting cusps for Occlusion, a bone for MSK 3, a flexed arm for MSK 4, a crown on a prep for PCD). On every leaderboard (rank, streak, correct-in-a-row, both arcades and Tooth Fairy collectors) one medal sits next to your name: the medal for the hub you're in, or your best one on the dashboard, then "+N" for the rest. Tap it to see all of someone's medals. Your rank card shows each one with its hub's name. A new medal gets its own card (below).

Trophy case: 27 trophies, in More → Stats and trophies in a hub, or from the Trophy case button on your card on the dashboard. Your rank sits on top with the road ahead. Then a showcase stand with one trophy at a time (it opens on your rarest; tap any trophy to put it there) and a cabinet with three shelves: Won by studying (8), The journeys (3: Handpiece, ModuPro and Loupes finished) and Secrets (16). A trophy you've won is lit on its brass plate with the share of the class that has it; one you haven't is dimmed, with what earns it; a secret you haven't found is only its shape and its clue, with how many have found it. Under those, a shelf for each hub with its own eight: the four mastery medals (Bronze, Silver, Gold and the Crown, in that hub's emblem), Seen It All, Mock Ace, Perfect Mock and a secret. If you won Full Arch before it was retired, it stays in your case on a "Retired" shelf. The leaderboards are behind the Leaderboards button.

Your stats: Under the case: your numbers on a scoreboard (answered, right, best run, days you met your goal), a card for each lecture with how you're doing (your strongest and the one that needs work marked), and your achievements.

Trophy and medal cards: A new trophy or medal pops up framed in its metal, drawn, with the share of the class that has it and what's next ("12 of 27 in your case", "Gold at 90% right"). A new rank names the pieces it brings to Timmy's place. They take turns, wait until a mock exam is submitted, are one still card with reduced motion, and are off with Settings → Extras → Rank-up and trophy cards.

Link my devices: Make a 6-character code on one device and enter it on another within 10 minutes; both then count as you (XP, streaks, trophies). Your question progress follows you too: questions you tried on your phone show up as tried (and right or missed) on your laptop the next time you open that hub, and the Daily Drill brings back misses from both. Answers you gave before linking come along. A hub also catches up when you come back to it after a few minutes away.

"Is this your other device?": If you save a name that another device already uses, you keep the name and a card asks whether that device is yours too. Tap "Yes, link them" and it shows a code and a link: send yourself the link and open it on your other device ("Link this device?", one tap), or type the code there (it links as soon as the sixth character is in). Or tap "No, that's someone else" and it won't ask about that name again. A device whose name is shared is also asked once a day until you answer ("Not now" waits 3 days).

sections.title: Timmy Tooth
items: Your cartoon tooth buddy. Everyone has one. Settings → Timmy Tooth: On, Dashboard only, or Off. Nobody else can see his health.

Everyone has Timmy: Nobody has to adopt him any more: he's there from your first visit, on the dashboard's You card and in the bottom-left corner of every hub, and he says hello. A Timmy you meet from the redesign on starts at full health, 100 HP; one you already had keeps his health and his history. Your other linked devices count his health from the day you first met him.
Where he lives: On the dashboard's You card, at his place (Timmy's place, below), and in the bottom-left corner of every hub with a health bar. He hides during mock exams.

Health: 0 to 100 HP, worked out from your answers in every hub. Each right answer heals 0.8 HP (up to 30 a day), each day in a row adds a streak bonus (up to 10), and each skipped day costs 8, then 12, 16 and 20 HP the longer you're away. At 0 he can't die, but he heals at half speed until he's back to 50.

What goes wrong: Below 70 HP: plaque. Below 55: brown stains and red, puffy gums (gingivitis). Below 40: a cavity. Below 25: periodontitis (recession, calculus, loose). Below 12: a cracked cusp. At 0: a bandage. Each goes away as he heals, and he thanks you.

Talking to him: Tap him for one of 73 dental jokes (plus holiday and fall jokes in season), a true tooth fact, one of his own thoughts, or a word about the outfit he's wearing; every few taps he gives a status update or a secret tip. "Tell me a joke" on the dashboard's You card is always a joke. Tap 5 times fast and he complains it tickles. "Checkup" opens his chart: health, today's answers, streak, and every condition. He deals his lines from shuffled decks, so you hear a whole set before any line comes back.

Ask Timmy: Tap Timmy and pick Ask me (on the dashboard, Ask me on the You card) to ask about the notes. He answers from the hub's own notes, review tables, Exam Hints and cram sheet only (on the dashboard, from every live hub's), in a few short lines, with a From the notes link under each point that opens the notes at that very paragraph. When the notes don't cover something he says so and points to the closest lecture. Starter questions: "What should I study tonight?" (he reads your own progress in the hub: weakest lectures, questions missed, lectures not started; it's worked out on your device and sent only with that question), "Explain this lecture simply" (while you're in its notes), "What's most likely on the exam?" and "How do I use this hub?" (on the dashboard, "When are my exams?" and "What can this site do?"). He won't answer a graded quiz, take-home or exam question, and gives no hints on a practice question before you've answered it. 40 questions a day; after that he naps until tomorrow. Paused during a mock exam. Thumbs up or down on each answer, Report on any answer that's wrong or odd (Sam sees the whole chat and replies in your Inbox), and past chats on this hub (the clock). Chats are saved to help improve the hub: see What the hubs record.

If he spots a problem or an idea: He writes it up for you: a report for Sam or an idea for the idea board, in a box you can edit. Nothing is sent until you tap Send (or Post); No thanks drops it. An idea goes up under your leaderboard name.
Ask Timmy on a question: After you answer a practice question, Ask Timmy under it opens the chat with that question attached ("Why is it ...?"). Not before you answer.

Timmy off?: When Timmy is turned off (Settings, Dashboard only on a hub, or Focus mode), an Ask button sits in his spot (a hub's bottom-left corner; the You card on the dashboard) and the same chat answers in a plain "Ask the hub" voice, with the same rules.
Secret tips: He tells you how to find every easter egg, one at a time. The "Secret tip" button on the dashboard's You card, every 4th tap, or sometimes as his hello in a hub.

Reactions: He greets you differently by time of day, day of the week and month, and notices what's going on: a skipped day or a long absence, your study streak, a big day of questions, a second visit, an exam within the week, his own place, and how long you've had him (one week, a month, 100 days and more). He cheers at 3, 5, 10 and more right in a row, winces at misses, encourages you after a bad run and celebrates the comeback, comments when you switch modes, reacts to every easter egg, naps if you go idle for 3 minutes, nudges you to take a break on long sessions, and gives pep talks the day before and the day of an exam.

Outfits: He wears what you put on him at his place (Customize → Timmy), from the shop or from your rank, and nothing when nothing is on: on the bar, on the dashboard, at his place, in the classroom and on the leaderboard's stage. Holiday looks are in the shop's seasonal sets. He no longer dresses himself for holidays.

Timmy's place: Timmy has a place of his own: a home, the scene around it and a yard with five spots. It is on the dashboard's You card and in every hub under More → Timmy's place. Tap the picture to step in: it opens like a small theater, the place on a gold-framed stage under a row of lights, with Timmy today beside it (how he is doing, his HP on a meter), your rank, your hub medals, and two buttons, Customize and Shop. Timmy at home: tap anything and he hops over to it; tap him and he waves, and again while he's waving for a flip. How he moves is his health: at 90 HP and up he bounces and wanders the most, lower down he slows, and when he needs treatment he stays on the doorstep and tells you what he needs. Studying is still what heals him. Your rank and your medals live there: a statue of your rank stands by the door, in your rank's metal, on one step for each level. Past the Handpiece the ModuPro joins it on the pedestal, and in the Loupes journey Timmy wears his loupes. Every hub you've earned a mastery medal in hangs its medal on the board by the house (up to twenty; tap the board to see them all, in each hub's colors). Customize: change the home, the scene, what stands in each yard spot, the home's upgrades and paint, and what Timmy wears, from what you own. Every change is saved as you make it and follows you to your other linked devices. The bowling lane is long: it takes the side yard and the front corner together. "Surprise me" picks a whole new look, the piece in use has a gold tick, and Done takes you back to the visit. What you own: the cottage on the hill is every Timmy's first home. Halloween 2026's set is a gift to everyone, each full rank-up gives an outfit and a yard piece (earned, never sold), and everything else is bought in Timmy's shop with Shiny Gold Crowns. What you own is yours for good, on every device you link; spending never lowers your XP or your rank. Seasons: the yard follows the year (spring blossom, fall leaves, winter snow), and on Timmy's holidays the place puts out its holiday props. Timmy himself wears what you put on him. The study-streak flame has two more colors: blue from 10 days in a row and Dark Matter from 30.

Timmy's shop: Shiny Gold Crowns are the hubs' money, for Timmy's shop. You earn 1 for every 10 XP (a boost's extra XP doesn't count), 25 for each trophy, 50 for each mastery medal and 20 for each rank-up. Spending them never lowers your XP or your rank. Your balance is on the dashboard's You card and on the shop's counter. The shop is on the dashboard's You card (the Shop button), in every hub under More, and from Timmy's place (its Shop button). Today's picks (four pieces, new at midnight Central time), This week (three, new every Monday), the seasons' sets while they're on, a "Back for today" shelf on two throwback days a month, and the snacks and boosts, always. Tap anything for a closer look; Buy asks once more, with your balance after. Outfits, homes, scenes, yard pieces and the home's upgrades are yours for good: "Put it on" or "Place it" takes you to the customizer. Rarity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic and Legendary, each with its own frame. The rarer a piece, the less often it's on a shelf. Today's showcase is the rarest piece on sale that you don't own yet. Snacks for Timmy: an apple (+10 HP), a cheese cube (+15), floss (+25) and a fluoride rinse (+40), one of each a day, and not while he's at 100 HP. He eats it at once. Studying still heals him too. Double XP boosts: one hour or three, starting when you buy one; a second one adds its time to the first. The 2x shows on your rank.

Visiting: Tap anyone on the dashboard's leaderboard (Ranks or Study streaks, the top three on the stage too) to fly over through the clouds to their Timmy's place: their home, scene and yard, what their Timmy is wearing, their rank's statue and their hub medals, under their leaderboard name. Tap their Timmy and he waves; the things around the place do what they do at yours. Your own row opens your own place. Visit someone random (under the leaderboard) rolls the die and takes you to anyone in the class who has decorated their place, on the leaderboard or not (never your own). Next rolls again, the back arrow returns to the places you've been, and you meet everyone once before anyone comes round twice. Top ten: visiting someone in the leaderboard's top ten shows their number next to their name: gold for #1, silver for #2, bronze for #3. Visiting from the leaderboard, the arrows on either side take you to the next or the last place on the board. Back to mine brings you home. What a visitor sees, and doesn't: only the place. Never your HP, XP as a number, your streak, your answers, your Shiny Gold Crowns, what you own beyond what's out, or when you did anything. Nobody can change your place but you, and there's no list of who visited. Everyone on a board can be visited (there's no switch to turn it off).
His trophies: Pearly Whites for getting him to 100 HP (a Timmy who starts at 100 has to slip below it first and come back); Full Recovery for bringing him from 0 back to 100.

sections.title: Easter eggs
items: None of them appear during a mock exam. Settings → Extras switches them off: the Golden Probe, Tooth Fairy, Plaque Boss and the nuke each have their own switch, Hidden secrets covers the rest, and All off turns everything off at once. Magic words can be typed anywhere on a hub page (not in a text box), or into the hub's Search box on a phone.
